title: Ask about every inference the text sets up
statement: Plan at least two inference points in every passage and ask a question that needs each one; an inference the text sets up that no question asks is decoration.
example: An audit counted 3 inference points in one lesson against the minimum of 2, each with its own question.
detail: The grade-3 rulebook's first question rule has every passage carry at least two inference points, a feeling or motive shown rather than stated, or a design choice in the writing worth interpreting, each cashed by a question that requires it. Shown-not-stated with no question is decoration, and a why question about a stated fact is recall in a costume. An audit of one lesson counted three such points, each cashed by its own question.

evidence.quote: **R1**: every passage carries ≥2 inference points — feeling/motive SHOWN not stated, or authorial design worth interpreting — and EACH is cashed by a question that requires it. Shown-not-stated with no question = decoration; a why about a stated fact = recall in a costume.
≥2 inference points, each cashed by a question — L4 carries 3
